newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down despite firm Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down despite firm Tokyo.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended the week lower in thin dealing despite a higher Tokyo's close, dealers said.

"Prices keep falling because of no demand. The summer holidays are over but buyers are not buying," a dealer said, adding that if the Europeans return to the market, they are likely to make enquiries for latex.
Dealers were offering SMR CV at 369-369 cents, SMR L at 348-349, SMR 5 at 318-320, SMR 10 at 308 and drum latex at between 237 and 240.
Dealers said lack of demand from China, who are seen buying in the Thai market where prices are at par or slightly cheaper, also dampened sentiment.
Ample supplies in the local market also weighed on prices, the dealers said.
At the close, October RSS 1 buyer fell 1.50 cents to 313.50 cents ($1.25) a kg and October SMR 20 buyer down a cent to 307.
The INRO five-day moving average was 245.32 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Sept 26 from 246.39 on Sept 25. The daily indicator price was 242.74 against 244.19.
